From: Beth Walters <beth.w@halo-analytics.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production spike and possible data loss - can you hold deletion window?

Hi Laura,

We hit a production incident this morning that may have caused a malformed payload to be stored against a small subset of user sessions (around ~120 sessions). Our infra team is collecting traces but we need Redwood to pause any automated deletion for the affected time range while we do forensics.

Request: can you place a short hold (48-72 hours) on deletion/auto-purge for any logs or traces tied to the Halo account between 2027-05-29T22:00Z and 2027-05-30T12:00Z? We only need the minimum data necessary for investigation.

I attached a screenshot of the error and the initial internal incident ticket ID (INF-4281). If you need a signed form or POA, we can get that over quickly.

Appreciate the quick help — this is impacting an ongoing regulatory investigation.

— Beth

Laura —
We can approve a short-term, narrowly scoped hold for an active security or compliance investigation, but it must meet the following (per policy):
1) Explicit scope (customer, time window, data types) — no blanket account-level holds
2) Duration limit (we should prefer 48 hours; 72 hours can be approved with sign-off)
3) Written customer acknowledgment and an internal ticket linking to an audit-hold form (signed POA or DocuSign)
4) Minimal export list — Ops should only produce a manifest of artifacts to be exported and Legal must review if data contains PII

Please ask Halo to sign the attached audit-hold-form.pdf and confirm the exact S3 bucket/regions if they want exports. Once we have the signed form, Legal will sign off for up to 72 hours.

Rishi Malhotra
Head, Security & Compliance
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Attachment: audit-hold-form.pdf (please have customer sign)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 17:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production spike and possible data loss - can you hold deletion window?

We can implement a timebound hold scoped to the Halo account and the exact UTC window requested. Operational constraints and plan:
- Hold window: 2027-05-29T22:00Z -> 2027-06-01T22:00Z (72 hours) — temporary; will auto-lift at end time
- Scope: logs, tracer fragments, and request/response payloads for session IDs matching the customer's supplied list (they must provide session ids or we will use account/time filters only)
- Exports: we will create a forensics export manifest and an encrypted export to the customer-specified S3 (must be in a supported region)
- Audit: every access during the hold will be logged and tagged to the INF-4281 investigation; Legal will get a copy of the manifest

I'll prepare the ops-checklist.md and a short forensics-manifest.txt. We will not change global retention settings; this is an isolated, ephemeral hold.

Olga Petrov
Sr. Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

Attachment: ops-checklist.md

Quick technical note from on-call:
- To minimize retained surface area I'll snapshot the KV cache and collect the per-request traces for the specified session ids only.
- Export will include: request timestamps, request payload (redacted where possible), response hashes, and server-side trace_ids. No full-user dumps.
- ETA to produce a prototype manifest: 6 hours after we have the signed audit-hold-form and the final session id list.

I'll attach the forensics-manifest.txt once generated and will coordinate SCP to their S3 endpoint.

— Dev Patel

Hi Beth — thanks for the quick context. We can place a timebound hold under the following conditions:

1) Scope & duration: hold applied only to Halo account artifacts between 2027-05-29T22:00Z and 2027-06-01T22:00Z for up to 72 hours (will auto-lift at end time).
